    Who was the 17 year old F1 driver?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The only 17-year-old to race in Formula 1 was Max Verstappen, who debuted in 2015 for Toro Rosso, making him the youngest driver ever at 17 years, 5 months, and 13 days old. While other young drivers like Oliver Bearman and Kimi Antonelli have debuted recently, they were 18, though a 2024 rule change allows for 17-year-olds with "outstanding ability".

    Key 17-Year-Old F1 Driver: 
    • Max Verstappen: Set the record in 2015, driving for Toro Rosso, and has since become a multiple-time World Champion for Red Bull Racing.
    Recent Young Drivers (Debuted at 18):
    • Oliver Bearman: Debuted for Ferrari at 18 years old in 2024. 
    • Arvid Lindblad: Became the third-youngest points scorer in 2026 at 18. 
    Rule Change for 17-Year-Olds: 
    • A rule change in 2024 allows the FIA to grant dispensation for 17-year-olds to race if they show "outstanding ability and maturity," paving the way for potential future teenage drivers like Kimi Antonelli.

      Why is Andrea Antonelli called Kimi?
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      Kimi Antonelli goes by Kimi because it's his actual middle name (full name: Andrea Kimi Antonelli) given to him by a family friend who thought the name suited him, and while he shares the name with Kimi Räikkönen, he wasn't named after the F1 champion, though the connection is a notable coincidence for fans. He prefers using Kimi over Andrea, as it's the name he's always been known by in racing, making it a natural choice for his public identity as a Formula 1 driver.
       
      You can watch this video to see some of the youngest pole-sitters in F1 history:

      • Not Named After Räikkönen:
        Antonelli has confirmed he wasn't named for the former F1 champion, though the parallel is striking. 
      • Preference:
        He prefers to be called Kimi, which has become his professional name in motorsport.

        Who is the youngest driver in F1?
        An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
        AI Overview
        The youngest Formula 1 driver ever to start a race is Max Verstappen, who made his debut at 17 years and 166 days old for Toro Rosso in 2015. He shattered the previous record, held by Jaime Alguersuari, and remains the youngest F1 driver on record, with other young talents like Kimi Antonelli and Arvid Lindblad recently making headlines for their own record-breaking starts.
         
        Key Youngest Driver Records (as of early 2026):
        • Youngest Starter: Max Verstappen (17 years, 166 days). 
        • Youngest Race Winner: Max Verstappen (18 years, 228 days at the 2016 Spanish GP). 
        • Youngest Pole Sitter (recent): Kimi Antonelli (19 years old at the 2026 Chinese GP). 
        Why This Matters:
        • Verstappen's debut was a significant moment, quickly followed by him becoming the youngest winner, podium finisher, and fastest lap setter in F1 history. 
        • Recent drivers like Antonelli and Lindblad continue to break records, showcasing the new era of young talent entering Formula 1.

          Italian Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli delivered a composed drive from pole position to claim his maiden Formula 1 victory at the Chinese Grand Prix, becoming the second youngest race winner in F1 history at 19 years and 202 days old and the first Italian to win a Grand Prix in 20 years since Giancarlo Fisichella’s 2006 Malaysian GP triumph. Antonelli displaced Sebastian Vettel from the record books, sitting behind only Max Verstappen as F1’s youngest winner, and finished 5.5 seconds ahead of teammate George Russell to secure Mercedes’ second consecutive one-two finish. Lewis Hamilton claimed third for his first Ferrari podium after battling Charles Leclerc, while reigning world champion Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri both failed to start due to McLaren electrical failures, and Max Verstappen retired from sixth with 10 laps remaining due to a Red Bull power unit issue.
